newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ICRC hopes prison committee will help end Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: ICRC hopes prison committee will help end Peru crisis.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Tuesday it hoped a commission set up by Peru to evaluate prison conditions would help resolve the hostage crisis.

The humanitarian agency also said it hoped the ad hoc governmental committee, in which it is not taking part, would lead to the resumption of regular ICRC prison visits, suspended since the hostage crisis began on December 17.
But in a statement, ICRC reaffirmed the standard terms for its prison visits -- access to all detainees, interviews without witnesses and the right to repeat visits.
The ICRC is providing aid to the 72 hostages being held by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) and has taken part in the negotiations between the rebels and the government.

Noting the setting up of the committee, it said: "The ICRC earnestly hopes that this will not only be a step forward in efforts to resolve the hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, but that it will also lead to an early resumption of ICRC visits to Peruvian penitentiary establishments.

"Despite repeated approaches, the ICRC has not yet been authorised to resume its activities for detainees," it said, adding that "no exception is made in any circumstance" to its standard terms for prison visits.
As of mid-December, ICRC delegates had been making visits to 4,247 detainees in Peru being held for "security reasons".

"On the basis of its observations, the ICRC submitted confidential reports to the Peruvian authorities drawing attention to matters that required improvement in light of the applicable provisions of international humanitarian law," it said. The Swiss-run ICRC declined to reveal its recommendations.
